newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen buoyed as favourites rotate.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen buoyed as favourites rotate.

text.p: German shares were expected to hold broadly firm in the short term, irrespective of Wall Street's fortunes, as new favourites emerge to replace stocks going out of vogue, dealers said on Thursday afternoon.

Car shares were in the spotlight as trading progressed, with Volkswagen AG advancing some four percent after several positive comments from analysts, including Merrill Lynch's reiteration of a "strong buy" recommendation.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index was down 11.05 points at 3,808.47 points, well off its intraday highs, but still holding firmly above the psychologically key 3,800 point level.
September DTB DAX futures were down 9.5 points at 3,830.5 points.
Profit-taking hit some shares, especially the banking sector, but that was offset by selective buy interest. In late trade, around a third of DAX 30 shares were higher and the rest were in decline.
"There is no solid trend here. First we went for Siemens, then Deutsche, then Veba VABG.F and now VW. There's always some favourite," said a Frankfurt trader.
Deutsche Bank, a top climber in recent days, was down 1.90 marks at 102.20 marks.
Siemens AG was also down 1.40 marks at 105.65 marks.
Shares in Volkswagen were up 49.95 marks, or four percent, at 1,299.05 marks, making them the strongest advancers in late trade.
Merrill Lynch analyst Stephen Reitman confirmed that he had reiterated his target of 1,700 marks for Volkswagen shares as well as his "strong buy" recommendation.
Other car shares were also higher, with Daimler-Benz AG up 1.40 marks at 142.50 marks.
The stable dollar, trading at 1.7280 marks in the afternoon, was supporting the car segment, dealers said.
The uptrend was seen as likely to continue in the short term as the end of the second quarter approaches, boosting liquidity.
No major negatives were on the horizon, dealers said, with the overall environment generally viewed as positive for shares.
No surprises came from the Bundesbank today, as the German central bank kept its key interest rates on hold as expected.
